items.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
items.author: Jian Gu, Hongyu Zhang, Chunyang Chen, Aldeida Aleti
items.description: The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does. We argue that…
items.summary: The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does.

items.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
items.author: Yijiang Li, Bingyang Wang, Nuno Vasconcelos
items.description: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only…
items.summary: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question.

items.title: The Pulse: new trend of building “internal vibe-coding apps” at tech companies
items.author: Ivan Klaric
items.description: Ramp and Stripe built platforms for non-engineers to build internal websites and tools with, and both are taking off in those workplaces. I expect more companies to do the same.

items.title: The next developer interface is ambient intelligence
items.author: Martin Woodward
items.description: AI, agents, voice, and physical controls are shifting software development from operating tools to expressing intent—and helping developers stay focused on building. The post The next developer interface is ambient intelligence appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.summary: For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools changed, but the relationship did not.
